test_policy.notes: ACT/SAT are generally not required for undergraduate admission, but scores are used for scholarship eligibility and may be needed for placement or specific programs; international applicants may submit them optionally. Admission decision is based on unweighted high school GPA.

requirements.notes: Apply on Morehead State's own online application. CDS C13 lists a $30 application fee (the international pages do not state a fee). Required: official high school transcript showing graduation, GPA of at least 2.50 (the Admission Requirements page also lists provisional admission for international students with a 2.00-2.49 GPA), English proficiency proof, original bank documents at least $43,125 (the Admission Requirements page says $34,000; confirm the current amount) on bank letterhead and under three months old, and passport/visa/I-20 copy. BSN nursing and imaging sciences need a second, program-level admission step. Federal rules require at least four face-to-face classes for F-1 students.

deadlines.label: International application deadline, fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Printed without a year, treated as fall 2027. Other terms: spring Jan. 2, winter Dec. 2, summer May 15 (based on course availability). CDS C14 lists a fall closing date of 8/24 and a priority date of 3/15 for all applicants.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: applicants from the listed English-speaking countries (e.g., Australia, Canada except Quebec, Ireland, Jamaica, New Zealand, UK, US and several Caribbean nations); graduates of a U.S. high school who submit ACT 20 or SAT 1030; or 24 or more credit hours from an accredited U.S., Australian, Canadian (not Quebec), Irish, New Zealand or UK institution. The pages do not mention conditional admission or an intensive English pathway.

english.notes: Also TOEFL 173 computer-based or 500 paper. Institution code 1487. The pages do not give a 1-6 scale value.
Duolingo English Test (official score), 105; listed on the international admission and requirements pages but not on the English proficiency page.
Pearson Test of English Academic, 50; listed on the international admission and requirements pages but not on the English proficiency page.

cost.notes: Rates effective July 1, 2026, full-time 12-18 credits, two semesters: Kentucky resident $5,201 per semester, out-of-state $7,840, international $13,120. Mandatory fees are $6 and $5 per credit hour capped at $66 and $60 per semester ($252 a year at the cap). Books: Eagle Books program $25 per credit hour (30 credits is $750). The international tuition page (undated) estimates living expenses of $12,954 for housing and meals, $8,850 for insurance and miscellaneous, and tuition and fees of $26,474, total $42,278; it is not used for room and board because it is undated.

aid.notes: International Student Scholarship: $8,000 a year ($4,000 per semester) for incoming international freshmen with an Admission Index of 450 or higher and ACT 20 or SAT 940 (the international scholarships page says 940; the Additional Scholarships page says SAT 1020 or higher); renewable with a 2.00 GPA; cannot be combined with the non-resident tuition scholarship or used for internet classes. International students may also apply for the competitive Honors Scholarship (tuition, on-campus housing, meal plan, book help). The CDS H6 policy checkboxes are not legible. International students are not eligible for federal aid.
